name: email-digest
title: Email Digest
description: A composed email — a branded frame, a written subject and message, the items worth the reader's attention, a sign-off.

files.components/body.yaml:
unoverse: "1.0"
# THE LETTER'S BODY — the main part an Agent writes: a greeting, the message itself, and
# the line that hands off to whatever the email is showing. Three separately briefed
# fields, because they are three different writing jobs and one description could not
# govern all of them.
#
# The message is drawn by a bound `Markdown` node rather than a `Ref` to the `prose`
# atom ON PURPOSE: a brief on a Ref never compiles, and the atom's own generic
# description would silently replace the one written here.
type: component
name: body
category: Communication
nodeSize:
  width: 600
  height: 320
props:
  greeting:
    type: string
    input: true
    description: >-
      The greeting, on its own line. The reader's first name and a comma when the
      source gives a name; a plain "Hello," when it does not. Never invent a name,
      never guess a title, and never add a line of small talk here.
    maxLength: 40
    default: Hi Sarah,
  message:
    type: string
    input: true
    description: >-
      The message: two or three short paragraphs saying why this email is being
      sent to THIS reader, in the second person. Ground every claim in what the
      source actually says about them; where it says nothing, write less rather
      than filling the space. Do not list or describe the individual items — they
      are shown below in their own right, and repeating them here reads as
      padding. Markdown paragraphs and inline marks only: no headings, no bullet
      lists, no links.
    default: |-
      Thanks for telling us where you want to take your career. Based on what you
      said about moving into practice and studying alongside work, I have pulled
      together a short list rather than the full catalogue.

      Each one is part time, starts this September, and is taught live with
      on-demand catch-up, so none of them assume you can drop everything.
  leadIn:
    type: string
    input: true
    description: >-
      One line handing off to the items shown below it — "Here is what I would
      look at first". It introduces them as a set; it never names, counts or
      ranks them, because what finally appears is chosen after this line is
      written.
    maxLength: 70
    default: Here is what I would look at first
root:
  type: Box
  style:
    direction: column
    gap: "4"
    width: full
  children:
    - type: Text
      bind:
        value: greeting
      style:
        font: body.md
        color: text.primary
    - type: Markdown
      bind:
        value: message
      style:
        width: full
    - type: Text
      bind:
        value: leadIn
      style:
        font: body.md
        weight: semibold
        color: text.primary
files.components/footer.yaml:
unoverse: "1.0"
# THE EMAIL FRAME'S FOOT — the sign-off, the reason-you-are-hearing-from-us line, and
# the regulatory wording. Same reason as email-masthead: BPP's hardcoded "BPP
# Education Group" could not ride a shelf template, so the words became data.
type: component
name: footer
category: Communication
nodeSize:
  width: 600
  height: 200
props:
  orgName:
    type: string
    description: "The organisation sending the email, as it should appear in the footer."
    input: false
    default: Your organisation
  note:
    type: string
    description: "Why this person is receiving the email, in one line."
    input: false
    default: You are receiving this because you asked to hear from us.
  legal:
    type: string
    description: "Any legal line the footer must carry, such as a registered address. Empty means none."
    input: false
    default: ""
root:
  type: Box
  style:
    direction: column
    gap: "2"
    padding: [ "5", "6" ]
    width: full
  children:
    - type: Text
      bind:
        value: orgName
      style:
        font: body.sm
        weight: semibold
        color: text.primary
    - type: Text
      visibleWhen: note
      bind:
        value: note
      style:
        font: body.sm
        lineHeight: snug
        color: text.secondary
    # COMPOSED, never hand-rolled: `fine-print` already owns what legal wording looks
    # like (quieter, smaller, its own top rule) and it is briefed to REPRODUCE the
    # source rather than rewrite it. `props` maps the atom's own `body` field onto
    # this component's `legal`.
    - type: Ref
      ref: fine-print
      visibleWhen: legal
      props:
        body: legal
files.components/items.yaml:
unoverse: "1.0"
# THE LETTER'S ITEMS: what the email is showing the reader, stacked one under another as a
# newsletter lists them. The Agent picks each item by ref from what its search found, and
# the item's own name, words, picture and link arrive with the result, so nothing about
# an item is ever written.
type: component
name: items
category: Communication
nodeSize:
  width: 600
  height: 900
props:
  items:
    type: array
    input: true
    description: >-
      The items worth this reader's attention, most relevant first, each one a result the
      search found, picked by its ref. Only what the source actually supports for this
      reader; fewer is better than a padded list.
    minItems: 1
    maxItems: 3
    preview:
      - title: Lightsaber Combat Training
        description: Master the seven forms of lightsaber combat with guidance from Jedi Masters.
        image: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1761403583/gravity/YodaPark/darth-vader-main_4560aff7.jpg
        link: "[BEGIN TRAINING](https://example.com)"
      - title: Starship Piloting Fundamentals
        description: Learn to fly by instruments and by feel, from first launch to a clean landing.
        image: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1761403583/gravity/YodaPark/darth-vader-main_4560aff7.jpg
        link: "[START FLYING](https://example.com)"
      - title: The Way of the Force
        description: A guided course in focus and patience, taught live with on-demand catch-up.
        image: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1761403583/gravity/YodaPark/darth-vader-main_4560aff7.jpg
        link: "[FIND OUT MORE](https://example.com)"
    items:
      title:
        type: string
        description: The item's own name, exactly as it is published. Comes from the referenced result.
        hydrate: title
        override: false
      description:
        type: string
        description: What the item is, in its own published words. Comes from the referenced result.
        hydrate: body
        override: false
      image:
        type: string
        description: The item's own picture, drawn from the referenced result. Never authored.
        hydrate: image
      link:
        type: string
        description: The way into this item, drawn from the referenced result. Never authored.
        hydrate: link
root:
  type: Each
  bind:
    items: items
  style:
    direction: column
    gap: "5"
    width: full
  item:
    type: Box
    style:
      width: full
      direction: column
      background: surface.base
      border: subtle
      shadow: lg
      overflow: hidden
      textAlign: start
    children:
      - type: Ref
        ref: cover-image
        visibleWhen: image
        props:
          src: image
          alt: title
      - type: Box
        style:
          direction: column
          padding: "6"
          gap: "3"
          align: start
        children:
          - type: Text
            bind:
              value: title
            style:
              font: headline.sm
              weight: semibold
              color: text.primary
          - type: Text
            visibleWhen: description
            bind:
              value: description
            style:
              font: body.md
              color: text.secondary
          - type: Ref
            ref: cta-link
            visibleWhen: link
            props:
              link: link
files.components/masthead.yaml:
unoverse: "1.0"
# THE EMAIL FRAME'S HEAD. It exists because a universal template cannot carry client
# words: BPP's intake email opened with a hardcoded "BPP / September intake" masthead,
# which is exactly the branding a shelf artifact may not hold. The words become DATA
# supplied at the use, and the ground comes from the org's own theme tokens — the
# cta-link rule, applied to the frame: the brand lives in tokens, never here.
type: component
name: masthead
category: Communication
nodeSize:
  width: 600
  height: 160
props:
  wordmark:
    type: string
    description: "The organisation's name as it reads at the top of the email."
    input: false
    default: Your organisation
  kicker:
    type: string
    description: "The short line above or beside the wordmark naming this edition."
    input: false
    default: This month's edition
root:
  type: Box
  style:
    direction: column
    gap: "3"
    padding: [ "6", "6" ]
    width: full
    background: surface.inverse
  children:
    - type: Text
      bind:
        value: wordmark
      style:
        font: headline.sm
        weight: semibold
        lineHeight: tight
        color: text.inverse
    # THE ACCENT RULE — a short stroke of the org's primary under the wordmark. It is
    # what stops the masthead reading as a plain dark bar, and it costs one token: an
    # org that rebrands gets a new rule for free.
    - type: Box
      style:
        width: "10"
        height: "1"
        radius: full
        background: action.primary
    - type: Text
      visibleWhen: kicker
      bind:
        value: kicker
      style:
        font: caption
        color: text.inverse
files.components/signoff.yaml:
unoverse: "1.0"
# THE LETTER'S SIGN-OFF — who sent it, after the items. Separate from the body
# because it sits on the far side of the item band: the reader sees what was sent
# before they see who sent it, which is the shape of a letter.
type: component
name: signoff
category: Communication
nodeSize:
  width: 600
  height: 160
props:
  closing:
    type: string
    input: true
    description: >-
      The closing line, offering the reader their next move in one sentence — how
      to reply, ask, or come back with questions. Only an action the source
      actually supports; never invent a phone number, a deadline or an offer.
    maxLength: 120
    default: Any questions, just reply to this email and it comes straight to me.
  senderName:
    type: string
    input: true
    description: >-
      The name the email is signed with, exactly as the source gives it. Blank
      when the source names no sender — an unsigned letter is better than an
      invented signature.
    maxLength: 60
    default: Jo Whitfield
  senderRole:
    type: string
    input: true
    description: >-
      The sender's role or team, as the source states it. Blank when it does
      not state one.
    maxLength: 60
    default: Course Adviser
root:
  type: Box
  style:
    direction: column
    gap: "3"
    width: full
    padding: ["6", "0", "0", "0"]
    borderTop: thin subtle
  children:
    - type: Text
      bind:
        value: closing
      style:
        font: body.md
        lineHeight: snug
        color: text.secondary
    - type: Box
      style:
        direction: column
        gap: "0"
        width: full
      children:
        - type: Text
          bind:
            value: senderName
          style:
            font: body.md
            weight: semibold
            color: text.primary
        - type: Text
          visibleWhen: senderRole
          bind:
            value: senderRole
          style:
            font: body.sm
            color: text.secondary
files.components/subject.yaml:
unoverse: "1.0"
# THE LETTER'S SUBJECT — the first part an Agent writes in the email-digest template.
# A BRIEFED component: the brief rides on the node that BINDS the field, which is the
# only place the schema compiler reads it from (design/CLAUDE.md §3).
type: component
name: subject
category: Communication
nodeSize:
  width: 600
  height: 120
props:
  subject:
    type: string
    input: true
    description: >-
      The subject line: what this email is about, in the reader's own terms. Say the
      benefit to them, not the sender's activity — "Three courses that fit where
      you're heading", never "Your September intake update". No greeting, no sender
      name, no colon-prefixed label, and never a question the email does not answer.
      Over the limit, write a shorter sentence; never abbreviate or drop characters
      to fit.
    maxLength: 78
    default: Three courses that fit where you're heading
root:
  type: Box
  style:
    direction: column
    gap: "2"
    width: full
  children:
    - type: Text
      bind:
        value: subject
      style:
        font: headline.md
        weight: semibold
        lineHeight: tight
        color: text.primary
files.email-digest.yaml:
unoverse: "1.0"
# THE SHELF'S EMAIL DIGEST (docs/unoverse/design/models/UNOVERSE_TEMPLATE_MODEL.md §9b).
# ONE flat state (owner ruling): an email is a document, not a surface you navigate;
# nothing rearranges while it is read. Everything else lives where it belongs: the parts
# placed in layouts/email in the letter's order, the template's own parts in
# components/ (the folder is the namespace), discovery meta in manifest.yaml.
type: template
name: email-digest
states:
  email:
    layout: layouts/email
files.layouts/email.yaml:
# THE EMAIL, one flat arrangement in the letter's order: masthead, subject, body
# copy, the items it is showing you, the sign-off, the small print. Each part is
# placed with a Ref (§9b), and each of its props' `input` says whether an Agent
# writes it. Nothing here opens, expands or rearranges.
#
# A MEASURED SHEET, centred. An email is a fixed-measure document, so the sheet caps
# at the named page width and centres in whatever it is placed in, rather than
# stretching to the host — the one cap layout.yaml sanctions by name. The cap is
# also what makes the item band read as a letter's list instead of a web page's grid.
type: Box
style:
  direction: column
  align: center
  width: full
children:
  - type: Box
    style:
      direction: column
      width: full
      maxWidth: page
      # THE MEASURING CONTEXT sits on the SHEET, not the host: anything inside that
      # asks how much room it has must be told the letter's width, never the screen's.
      container: inline-size
      background: surface.base
      border: thin subtle
      radius: lg
      shadow: sm
      overflow: hidden
    children:
      # THE MASTHEAD — the sender's frame, full-bleed to the sheet's edges (its own
      # padding is its business, which is why this line adds none).
      - type: Ref
        ref: components/masthead

      # THE LETTER — subject, then the copy. This is the block the reader actually
      # reads, so it gets the sheet's most generous margins and the widest gaps.
      # Blank is valid: the items settle in ~300ms and the prose lands into this
      # reserved space seconds later, so the column holds its shape while empty.
      - type: Box
        style:
          direction: column
          gap: "5"
          padding: [ "8", "8", "6", "8" ]
          width: full
        children:
          - type: Ref
            ref: components/subject
          - type: Ref
            ref: components/body

      # THE ITEM BAND — what the letter is showing you, STACKED. A newsletter lists
      # its items one under another; columns here would read as a web page, and at
      # the sheet's capped measure they would be too narrow to carry a card anyway.
      - type: Box
        style:
          direction: column
          gap: "5"
          padding: [ "0", "8", "7", "8" ]
          width: full
        children:
          - type: Ref
            ref: components/items

      # THE SIGN-OFF — after the items, as in a letter: the reader sees what was
      # sent before they see who sent it.
      - type: Box
        style:
          direction: column
          padding: [ "0", "8", "8", "8" ]
          width: full
        children:
          - type: Ref
            ref: components/signoff

      # THE SMALL PRINT — on a sunken ground so the sheet reads as ending rather
      # than simply stopping.
      - type: Box
        style:
          width: full
          background: surface.sunken
          borderTop: thin subtle
        children:
          - type: Ref
            ref: components/footer
files.manifest.yaml:
